```{r}
library(dplyr)
```
## 1. Import data
```{r}
#Creating a fuction to read in data
#The data files are in ASCII text, tab delimited
read_tab <- function(file) {
  read.delim(file.path("Data", file), sep = "\t", header = TRUE,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE,
             na.strings = "NA", strip.white = TRUE)
}
#Using the function to import data
macro_orig <- read_tab("Macroplot_data.txt")
macro      <- read_tab("Macroplot_data_Rev.txt")
micro      <- read_tab("Microplot_data.txt")
sites      <- read_tab("Site_variables.txt")
splist     <- read_tab("Species_list.txt")
```

## 2. Check the imported data
Exploring the data frames

### 2.1 Macroplot data
```{r}
# structural overview
glimpse(macro_orig)
```
```{r}
glimpse(macro)
```
Individual botanical identifications and girth data for 61965 individuals of 400 tree and liana species (including one unidentified category) with gbh ≥ 10 cm in 96 1-ha macroplots.

Checking how macro tables differ
```{r}
identical(names(macro_orig), names(macro)) #are columns the same?
all.equal(macro_orig, macro)               #short summary of differences
```
Result shows that both files have the same number of rows in the same order but 91 trees have a different species code.
Looking into which SpCode was changed.
```{r}
changed <- which(macro_orig$SpCode != macro$SpCode) #which SpCode code from tables doesnt match

#change results to df
sp_changes <- data.frame(
  PlotID   = macro$PlotID[changed],
  SpCode_orig = macro_orig$SpCode[changed],
  SpCode_rev  = macro$SpCode[changed]
)

#how many trees per "old -> new" pair, and in how many plots
sp_changes %>%
  count(SpCode_orig, SpCode_rev, name = "n_trees") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_trees)) #sort to look at the biggest change

sp_changes %>%
  group_by(SpCode_orig, SpCode_rev) %>%
  summarise(n_trees = n(), n_plots = n_distinct(PlotID),
            plots = paste(unique(PlotID), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
#Are the new codes in the species list?
setdiff(unique(sp_changes$SpCode_rev), splist$SpCode)
```
Every corrected species code exists in Species_list.txt, so the revised file is consistent with the species list. 

```{r}
#Were the OLD codes perhaps not in the species list? (would explain the correction)
setdiff(unique(sp_changes$SpCode_orig), splist$SpCode)

#Are ALL species codes in the revised macroplot and microplot data in the list?
setdiff(unique(macro$SpCode), splist$SpCode)
setdiff(micro$SpCode, splist$SpCode)
```
The original file had 6 invalid codes: Artogoss, Ficudrpu, Ipomsp., Lantcaac, Lepideci and Neurmalb. None of them are in the species list.

**We continue using the revised data ("Macroplot_data_Rev.txt").**
